verdict.rationale: Algolia's docs state that typo tolerance works out of the box and that there are ways to customize how tolerant search should be. Hands-on users independently praise the typo handling (comm-16, comm-18). One user wishing fuzzy matching could be turned off in some cases is a feature wish, not a concrete contradiction of documented tunability. missing for 10: specific documentation of the tuning controls (e.g., per-attribute or per-query toggles, word-length thresholds, number of typos allowed), and independent corroboration that the tuning works as described.

support.subject: As a developer, searches tolerate typos and misspellings out of the box, with tunable rules for when and how fuzzy matching applies

citations.quote: Algolia provides typo tolerance out-of-the-box, along with some important ways to customize just how tolerant a search experience should be.
Typo tolerance lets users make mistakes while typing but still find the they’re looking for.
They say the typo tolerance alone makes Algolia the best third-party search service.
